title: Marriage Allowance
summary: Marriage Allowance lets a spouse or civil partner transfer £1,260 of their Personal Allowance to their partner if they earn less than the Personal Allowance and the partner is a basic-rate taxpayer. Confirm eligibility and the tax year on GOV.UK.

title: Tax on dividends
summary: Dividends above the Dividend Allowance are taxed at dividend tax rates which differ from employment income rates. The Dividend Allowance and rates can change by tax year — always confirm the current figures on GOV.UK before relying on them.

title: Student loan repayments
summary: Student loan repayments are usually collected through PAYE or Self Assessment once income is above the plan-specific threshold. Different plans (for example Plan 1, Plan 2, Plan 4, Postgraduate) have different thresholds. Check GOV.UK for your plan.

title: High Income Child Benefit Charge
summary: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge. The charge can reduce Child Benefit; at higher incomes it can remove the benefit entirely. Confirm thresholds on GOV.UK for the tax year.

title: Company directors and Self Assessment
summary: Company directors often need to complete a Self Assessment tax return, for example for dividends, benefits, or other untaxed income. Corporation Tax for the company is separate from the director’s personal Self Assessment. Confirm on GOV.UK.

title: Employment expenses claim
summary: Employees may claim tax relief on certain unreimbursed job expenses if they were necessary for work and not covered by the employer. Rules are strict — check GOV.UK for what qualifies and how to claim.

title: Approved mileage allowance payments
summary: If you use your own car for business, approved mileage allowance payments (AMAPs) set HMRC rates for tax-free mileage payments. Cars and vans commonly use 45p per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in a tax year and 25p thereafter — confirm current rates on GOV.UK.

title: Pension tax relief overview
summary: Most people get tax relief on pension contributions. Relief depends on how you pay in (relief at source, net pay, or Self Assessment) and on annual allowance rules. Confirm details for your scheme on GOV.UK.

title: Gift Aid
summary: Gift Aid lets charities claim basic-rate tax on donations. Donors must pay enough UK Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax to cover the tax the charity reclaims. Higher-rate taxpayers may claim extra relief via Self Assessment or PAYE.

title: Capital allowances overview
summary: Capital allowances let businesses claim tax relief on certain equipment and assets instead of deducting the full cost as an expense. Annual Investment Allowance and other reliefs may apply — confirm current limits on GOV.UK.

title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme
summary: The VAT Flat Rate Scheme lets eligible small businesses pay VAT as a percentage of turnover. Eligibility and percentages depend on business type. Confirm whether the scheme suits you on GOV.UK — it is not suitable for every business.

title: Corporation Tax overview
summary: Limited companies pay Corporation Tax on profits. Rates and thresholds can change by financial year. Company tax is separate from the directors’ personal Income Tax and Self Assessment. Confirm current rates on GOV.UK.

title: Scottish Income Tax
summary: If you live in Scotland, Scottish Income Tax rates and bands set by the Scottish Government apply to non-savings, non-dividend income. They differ from the rest of the UK. Always check the Scottish rates for the tax year on GOV.UK.

title: Off-payroll working (IR35) overview
summary: Off-payroll working rules (often called IR35) affect people who provide services through their own limited company. Medium and large clients usually decide employment status for tax. Confirm current rules and responsibilities on GOV.UK — this is a complex area.

title: PAYE overview
summary: Pay As You Earn (PAYE) is how HMRC collects Income Tax and National Insurance from employment income. Having PAYE tax deducted does not always mean you avoid Self Assessment if you have other untaxed income.

title: National Minimum Wage and National Living Wage
summary: UK employers must pay at least the National Minimum Wage or National Living Wage for the worker’s age band. Rates usually change each April. Confirm current hourly rates on GOV.UK — this is employment law as well as payroll.

title: VAT schemes overview
summary: Besides standard VAT accounting, HMRC offers schemes such as Flat Rate, Cash Accounting, and Annual Accounting for eligible businesses. Choosing a scheme affects how you account for VAT — check eligibility on GOV.UK.

title: Self Assessment payment deadlines
summary: Balancing payment for Self Assessment is normally due by 31 January following the tax year. Payments on account are usually due by 31 January and 31 July. Confirm your personal payment schedule in your HMRC account or on GOV.UK.

title: Blind Person's Allowance
summary: Blind Person’s Allowance is an extra tax-free allowance for people who meet HMRC’s criteria relating to blindness or severe sight impairment. Confirm the amount for the tax year on GOV.UK.

title: Tax on savings interest
summary: Interest from savings can be tax-free within Personal Savings Allowance limits, which depend on whether you are a basic, higher or additional-rate taxpayer. Confirm current allowances on GOV.UK.
